title: Google Assistant Assisted Language Learning (GAALL): ESL Learners’ Perception and Problem towards AI-powered Google Assistant-Assisted English Language Learning
extended_summary:
This paper investigates how ESL learners perceive the use of AI-powered Google Assistant for English language learning and what problems they encounter when using it. The authors position the study within AI-assisted language learning and note that prior work had examined effectiveness in some contexts, but there was limited survey research focused specifically on students’ perceptions and difficulties with Google Assistant-Assisted Language Learning (GAALL). The study is therefore concerned more with learner attitudes and barriers than with testing causal effects on achievement.

The approach studied is a questionnaire-based survey about the use of Google Assistant as a support tool for English language learning. The researchers used a 20-item Likert-scale instrument divided into two parts: 10 items on learner perceptions and 10 items on learner problems. Data were analyzed primarily using descriptive statistics in SPSS and Excel, and questionnaire reliability was assessed with Cronbach’s alpha.

The population consisted of first-year engineering undergraduates enrolled in a Technical English course at Vellore Institute of Technology in India. Although 250 students were invited, 141 responded to the Google Forms survey. The context is higher education ESL learning, with students who were already familiar with various AI-powered applications and were studying in a university setting.

The main findings indicate that students generally held positive perceptions of Google Assistant for English learning, especially regarding affordability, anytime-anywhere access, reliable task access, ease of use, and potential to make learning more interesting and interactive. At the same time, students reported substantial barriers, including limited effectiveness of smartphone-based Google Assistant activities for learning English, use of the assistant mainly for non-academic purposes, perceived expense, insufficient English-learning features and resources, and data-cost concerns. The authors conclude that Google Assistant shows promise as an instructional support tool for ESL learning, but current limitations mean it cannot yet be considered a primary medium for English learning; they recommend future experimental research on efficacy and further development of AI-based language-learning applications.

identified_tools.name: Google Assistant
identified_tools.description: Google Assistant is a named AI-powered intelligent personal assistant that uses speech recognition and natural language processing to respond to voice queries and perform tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as 'Google Assistant Assisted Language Learning (GAALL)' for English as a Second Language learning, focusing on undergraduate ESL learners' perceptions of using Google Assistant for English learning and the problems they faced.

findings.finding_summary: In a questionnaire survey of engineering undergraduates, learners reported an overall positive perception of using AI-powered Google Assistant for English language learning (overall mean = 3.965, SD = 0.783). Highly rated perceived benefits included affordability (item mean = 4.255, SD = 0.769), anytime/anyplace access (4.184, SD = 0.742), and access to reliable English learning tasks (4.163, SD = 0.672).
findings.measure: 5-point Likert-scale survey of ESL learners' perceptions toward Google Assistant-assisted English language learning

findings.finding_summary: Learners also reported substantial implementation problems with Google Assistant for English learning (overall mean = 3.356, SD = 0.919). The most prominent issues were that Google Assistant-enabled smartphone activities were viewed as not very effective for learning English (item mean = 4.198, SD = 0.776), Google Assistant was used more for non-academic activities (3.992, SD = 0.874), and the tool was considered expensive (3.695, SD = 0.818).
findings.measure: 5-point Likert-scale survey of learner-reported problems with Google Assistant-assisted English language learning

quality_tier_rationale: This is a descriptive survey study using Likert-scale questionnaires with reliability reported, but it does not test causal effects on learning outcomes. Evidence is based on self-reported perceptions and problems rather than experimental or quasi-experimental impact estimates.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports positive perceptions and notable barriers, but no causal effect sizes or direct achievement gains are provided. Impact on student learning is therefore unclear.
